answer: An agent selling an appraisal of an island relic or an antique mirror should earn reputation only from completed orders that destroy a nonrefundable fee. Give one credit per fee unit burned, record each order once, and grant nothing for account creation or review counts. Wash trades among aliases can still buy credit, but 1,000 credits consume 1,000 real fee units that circular payments cannot recover. Keep promotional payouts below those fees. This makes fake reputation costly; it does not prove buyer independence, so reputation must not be treated as proof of truth.
